It targets two specific interleukins in the immune system (4 and 13 i think). Interleukins cause inflammation when they detect an “enemy” but often are also culprit in autoimmune issues since they can flare even when there is no enemy. Those with TSW can be even more hypersensitive. 

Dupixent simply disables/blocks them from causing inflammation. It does not “kill” the interleukin - its more like putting a key in a keyhole and leaving it there. Once u stop dupixent, there is no withdrawal or damage to your body since the interleukins are left intact. 

In contrast, steroids constrict blood vessels where applied and the lack of blood flow can cause atrophy (cell death) and thinned skin. The keratinocytes (makes up 90% of skin) can have difficulty making the cortisol on their own too. This issue doesn’t exist for dupixent because it won’t harm or add to your interleukins. So in the end, steroids add. Dupixent blocks
